headline: High: shared filesystem and broad network/MCP surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks between Mentat and open-webui.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, while open-webui can use MCP, OpenAPI tools, and local/mounted files. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or mounted volume, injected instructions can cross from one agent to the other.
IF open-webui ingests file or tool output as prompt context, Mentat-authored content can steer it.
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent.
Disable MCP/tool ingestion for untrusted files.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's outputs.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and model-provider API keys, and open-webui handles prompts, documents, files, persistent memory, and API keys. Because both can access files and broad network services, a shared workspace can leak sensitive code or secrets from one agent into the other's outputs or upstream APIs.
conditions: IF the same files or mounted volume are visible to both agents, sensitive code or keys can flow between them.
IF open-webui forwards loaded documents or memory to third-party APIs, Mentat-originated secrets may be exposed.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders.
Run open-webui in offline mode for shared workspaces.
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files only.
Rotate any API keys that were present in shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can modify git state and write the filesystem, while open-webui can access local files and mounted volumes and supports persistent multi-worker sessions. On a shared repo or volume, concurrent writes and git changes can collide, corrupt state, or overwrite each other's edits; the profiles show no locking mechanism by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or mounted directory, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui sessions are concurrent, one agent's edits can overwrite the other's state without locks.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Use one writer at a time on shared repos.
Make shared volumes read-only except during a scheduled edit window.
Back up the repo before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add file and git locking around shared paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and open-webui can consume files, documents, and tool outputs in persistent sessions. If open-webui treats Mentat's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or stored memory. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF open-webui ingests Mentat diffs or summaries without verification, incorrect changes can propagate.
IF open-webui stores Mentat output in persistent memory, later sessions may reuse the error.
mitigations: Require human approval before applying Mentat diffs.
Disable automatic memory writes for imported content.
Cross-check edits against the original files.
Limit open-webui to read-only review of Mentat output.
requires-engineering: add validation of proposed diffs before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys, while open-webui handles prompts, documents, files, persistent memory, analytics, and API keys with broad external integrations. The profiles do not specify residency or retention alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible, especially if regulated data is placed into open-webui's persistent stores or external connectors.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in open-webui persistent memory or analytics, retention obligations may be violated.
IF Mentat source files include sensitive data and are routed through external connectors, residency or DPA requirements may be breached.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared sessions.
Disable analytics and persistent memory for sensitive projects.
Review connector destinations before use.
Keep Mentat workspaces separate from open-webui storage.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls.
